subject: ARA
label: Grade 02
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 02 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Short words and sentences
modules.outcome: read and write short words and sentences
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Short words and sentences', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and write short words and sentences. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Short words and sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and write short words and sentences, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: هذا كتاب. هذه قطة. أنا أحب مدرستي. (This is a book. This is a cat. I love my school.) Method: Model run for 'Short words and sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and write short words and sentences: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, warm up: say or read the example aloud twice, slowly. Cover it and say it again from memory.
Step 2, find the pattern: underline the word, ending or sentence part that 'Short words and sentences' is about. Say in your own words why it is there.
Step 3, change one thing: swap one word, name or number in the example and say the new version aloud.
Step 4, write two new lines of your own that do the same job. Keep them short and true to your life.
Step 5, swap with a partner: read each other's lines, circle one thing to fix, and fix it.
Step 6, own it: read your final lines to the class or teacher. Standard: read and write short words and sentences.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Short words and sentences), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Songs and short stories) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
